ITQAN:v2p367/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p367/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p367/r2.claim: يدع means to push an orphan away from his right; Abu Talib’s verse is cited as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p367/r2.anchor: قال يدفعه عن حقه أما سمعت قول أبي طالب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r3.claim: The unnamed leader is recognizable as Abū Lahab, who controlled the House's financial resources when the sūrah was revealed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r3.anchor: not addressed by name, yet it is quite evident that Ab ū Lahab’s character is under discussion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r7.claim: The description aims to expose the inner nature that causes his hard-hearted treatment of orphans.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r7.anchor: it unfolds his internal nature that is actually the cause of this callousness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r3.claim: The verb da‘a means to push and shove, as in the description of the condemned being shoved into Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r3.anchor: means “to push and shove,” as is used in S ūrah al-Ṭūr

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r4.claim: The Qur’an commands respect for orphans and rebukes those who fail to honour them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r4.anchor: orphans should be treated with regard and respect. It rebukes those who disregard them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r5.speaker: Abū Bakr (rta)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r5.claim: Abū Bakr said that in an Islamic society the weak remain strongest and most influential until they receive their rights.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r5.anchor: the caliph Ab ū Bakr (rta) once said, the weak are the strongest and the most influential unless they are given their rights

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r6.claim: People should deeply respect those who have yet to receive their rights, uphold their cause, and strive to secure those rights.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r6.anchor: every person of a society is required to deeply respec t the people who are yet to receive their rights

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.claim: The passage is attributed to Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿUmar ibn ʿĀʾidh, two hypocrites, or Abū Sufyān, who struck an orphan asking for food after his weekly sacrifice; Ibn Jurayj gives the last report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.anchor: ونزلت في أبي جهل، أو الوليد بن المغيرة، أو العاصي بن وائل، أو عمر بن عائذ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r5.claim: The majority read yadaʿʿu with a ḍamma and doubled ʿayn; ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and others read it lighter, meaning to leave the orphan without kindness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يدع بضم الدال وشد العين وعلي والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني: بفتح الدال وخف العين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r8.speaker: إبراهيم ابن عرفة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r8.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿArafa says the denier withholds the orphan's right; Mujāhid says he denies the right and does not feed him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r8.anchor: وقال إبراهيم ابن عرفة: يدع اليتيم: يدفعه عن حقه. وقال مجاهد: يدفعه عن حقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers an alternative syntax joining fa-dhālika to the one who denies judgment, omitting the answer to araʾayta, and making the woe to praying hypocrites a description standing for their pronoun; generic singular carries a plural sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.anchor: وطريقة أخرى أن يكون فذلك عطفا على الذي يكذب، إما عطف ذات على ذات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's accusative parsing of fa-dhālika strange and unnatural: a nominative subject is immediate, while an accusative would require repeating the verb and pointing needlessly to the person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.anchor: فجعل فذلك في موضع نصب عطفا على المفعول، وهو تركيب غريب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.claim: The author says a more idiomatic construction would coordinate a following relative clause or use a verb directly, rather than insert the demonstrative in al-Zamakhsharī's proposed parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.anchor: بل الفصيح أكرمت الذي يزورنا فالذي يحسن إلينا، أو أكرمت الذي يزورنا فيحسن إلينا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.claim: He rejects the proposed parsing that makes the demonstrative refer to a separate entity: fa-dhālika points back to the one who denies, so they are not two entities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.anchor: فلا يصح، لأن فذلك إشارة إلى الذي يكذب، فليسا بذاتين

FARRA:v3p294#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p294#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p294#2/r2.claim: Yaduʿ means pushing an orphan away from his right and wronging him; the same root describes pushing people toward Hell.
FARRA:v3p294#2/r2.anchor: من دععت وهو يدع: يدفعه عن حقه، ويظلمه. وكذلك: «يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم » .

BINTSHATI:v2p192/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r3.claim: The Quran extends responsibility beyond private worship: rejecting the orphan and failing to urge food for the poor counts as denying the religion and neglecting public solidarity and mercy.
BINTSHATI:v2p192/r3.anchor: بل يعد دع اليتيم وعدم الحض على طعام المسكين تكذيباً بالدين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.claim: He notes that people affiliated with Islam may push an orphan from his rights or fail to care for him, discourage feeding the poor, neglect prayer, show off, and withhold zakat or necessities.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7.anchor: كدع اليتيم , وهو دفعه عن حقه وعدم الرفق به , وعدم الحض على طعام المسكين , والتغافل عن الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.claim: He reads these traits as those of a denier who expects no judgment, while observing that such acts can occur among Muslims without every person who commits them necessarily being a denier.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8.anchor: فأخبر سبحانه وتعالى أنه من صفات من يكذب بيوم الدين ولا ينتظر الجزاء والحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9.claim: The author compares this trait-based description to hadiths that call one with four specified traits a pure hypocrite and say a fornicator is not a believer while committing the act.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.claim: Al-Anfal 8:4 describes true believers as those who establish prayer and spend from God's provision, connecting with al-Ma'un's themes of prayer and giving.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r1.anchor: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r4.claim: Yaduʿu means to push the orphan harshly, either by denying care or usurping property and rights, the latter being worse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r4.anchor: ودع اليتيم: دفعه بعنف، وذلك إما أن يكون المعنى عن إطعامه والإحسان إليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r5.claim: Abu Raja reads yaduʿu with light dal and the sense of failing to treat the orphan well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء: «يدع» ، بفتح الدال خفيف بمعنى لا يحسن إليه،

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada classify the seven-verse sura as Meccan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.speaker: الضحاك، الواقدي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Waqidi classify the sura as Medinan.

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.claim: Muqatil says it is Meccan through the mention of the needy, with the remainder Medinan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.anchor: مكية إلى قوله: (المسكين) وباقي السورة مدنية، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.claim: A report transmitted from Ubayy says reciting this sura brings God's forgiveness for one who pays zakat; no grading is given.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (أرأيت) غفر الله له

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.claim: After recounting favors to Quraysh, the sura marvels at their conduct despite Meccan security and provision, then their denial of the Prophet and his prophethood.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.anchor: افتتح هذه السورة تعجبا من حالهم مع عظم النعم عليهم بمكة من الأمن والرزق

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r6.claim: The common reading yaduʿ has a doubled ʿayn and means to push away forcefully.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r6.anchor: قراءة العامة: (يدع) بضم الدال وتشديد العين من الدع، وهو الدفع

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r7.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r7.claim: Abu Raja reads yaduʿ with an open dal and light ʿayn, meaning to leave or abandon, from wadaʿa.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: يدع بفتح الدال، وتخفيف العين أي: يترك، من قولهم: ودعته أي: تركته

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r8.claim: The claim that Arabic lacks this verb's past tense and verbal noun is false; the Prophet's wording uses wadaʿ as a noun for leaving Friday prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r8.anchor: فقد ورد في الحديث: لينتهين الناس عن ودعهم الجمعات أو ليختمن على قلوبهم

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r9.claim: An unnamed poet's waddaʿahu means that he left his beloved, further attesting the verb.

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r11.claim: Al-daʿ means forceful pushing; related uses evoke shaking a measure to fill it, urging an unsteady person, or driving goats.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r11.anchor: الدع: الدفع بشدة، دععته دعا، ودعه يدعه دعا: إذا دفعته دفعا شديدا

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r12.claim: The root also appears in moving a measure so it fills, telling someone who stumbles daʿ daʿ, and as a goatherd's urging sound.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r12.anchor: الدعدعة: تحريكك المكيال ليستوعب الشيء، كأنه يدفعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r9.claim: Mujahid says the person who pushes the orphan treats him with contempt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r9.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى يحقر البيت , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says he wrongs the orphan.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r11.claim: The verb can mean pushing the orphan forcefully; Mawardi cites another verse's use of it for people driven into Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r11.anchor: الثالث : يدفع اليتيم دفعا شديدا , ومنه قوله تعالى : { يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا }

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r12.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says the orphan is pushed away from his right and deprived of his property out of injustice and greed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r12.anchor: يدفعه عن حقه ويمنعه من ماله ظلما له وطمعا فيه , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r13.claim: The orphan may instead be pushed away to humiliate and rebuke him; a lighter reading means leaving him unattended, or using and oppressing him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r13.anchor: يدفعه إبعادا له وزجرا , وقد قرىء ( يدع اليتيم ) مخففة , وتأويله على هذه القراءة يترك اليتيم

MUQATIL:107:1-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r3.claim: The orphan-denier pushes the orphan away from his due and withholds it; Muqatil links this wording to 52:13.
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r3.anchor: يعنى يدفعه عن حقه، فلا يعطيه، نظيرها: يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم [الطور: 13]

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.anchor: commentators maintain that al-Māʿūn is an early Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.anchor: Nonetheless, hypocrisy in religion was not seen as limited to Muslims alone.

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.claim: The surah warns people professing religion whose traits resemble hypocrites: neglecting prayer, acting ostentatiously, and withholding aid, all incompatible with belief in requital.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد لمن كان من المنتحلين بالدين متخلقا بأخلاق المنافقين

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan; another view says its first half is Meccan and second half Medinan.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، وقيل نصفها مكي ونصفها مدني

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r5.claim: Da' means to repel harshly and rudely; the fa in 'that is' implies a conditional inference describing how denial of requital appears in orphan mistreatment.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r5.anchor: الدع هو الرد بعنف وجفاء، والفاء في { فذلك } لتوهم معنى الشرط والتقدير

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r6.claim: The denier shoves the orphan away and shows no fear of consequences; if he feared them, he would treat the orphan mercifully.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r6.anchor: فذلك الذي يرد اليتيم بعنف ويجفوه ولا يخاف عاقبة عمله السيء

ELMALILI:107:2-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r1.claim: The opening fa links this description causally or as the answer to an omitted condition; the definite predicate restricts the referent to people who deny judgment.
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r1.anchor: Fâ, sebebiyye veya şart-ı mahzûfun cevâbı olarak

ELMALILI:107:2-7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r2.claim: The denier of judgment harshly shoves and drives away the orphan, exploiting the child's weakness without mercy or fear of God.
ELMALILI:107:2-7/r2.anchor: insaf ve merhamet etmeyerek kakar kakıştırır, kahr u hakāretle kovar azarlar

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r3.claim: The imperfect verbs indicate habitual conduct; the surrounding context condemns people who, despite rescue from hunger and fear, fail their duties of worship and mutual care for orphans and the hungry.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r3.anchor: يَدُعُّ، وَلَاَ يَحُضُّ fiilleri istimrar ifade eder muzâri‘olmak hasebiyle bu âyetlerin yukarıya rabtından çıkan mânanın hâsılı şu olur

ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r4.claim: Rejecting the orphan and ignoring the poor are habitual traits of those who deny religion; once faith is denied, such cruelty is unsurprising, while its appearance among the devout is more astonishing.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#2/r4.anchor: böyle yetimi kakmak ve fukarâya bakmamak gibi insafsızlıklar dine yalan diyen kimselerin yapageldikleri âdeti, huyu demektir

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.claim: Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1.anchor: namaz kılar dindar görünüp de namazlarından yanılan, mürâîlik, gösteriş yapıp

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r2.claim: Sūrat al-Māʿūn explains the preceding Sūrat Quraysh; its wording 'woe' and its meaning of withholding aid then connect it to Sūrat al-Humaza.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r2.anchor: Mâ‘ûn Sûresi ile tavzih olunarak buradan “veyl” kelimesi ile lafzen

ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.claim: After the address to the Prophet to see and understand, Sūrat al-Kawthar condenses the preceding suras, especially those from al-Ḍuḥā, as a final account of Muhammad's rank.
ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r3.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelerin mazmûnu üzerinde hepsinin tetimmesi

BURSEVI:v10p403/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r2.claim: The denier violently shoves and rudely rebukes the orphan.
BURSEVI:v10p403/r2.anchor: {فذالك الذى يدع اليتيم} أي بدفعه دفعا عنيفا

BURSEVI:v10p403/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r3.claim: A report says Abū Jahl was guardian to an orphan who came naked seeking his own money; he pushed the boy away, and Quraysh mockingly sent him to seek Muhammad's help.
BURSEVI:v10p403/r3.anchor: كان وصيا ليتيم فجاءه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه

BURSEVI:v10p403/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r4.claim: The Prophet accompanied the boy to Abū Jahl, who paid him; when Quraysh accused him of converting, he said he had feared a spear appearing beside Muhammad would strike him.
BURSEVI:v10p403/r4.anchor: فذهب معه إلى أبي جهل فقام أبو جهل وبذل المال لليتيم فعيره قريش وقالوا أصبوت

BURSEVI:v10p403/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r5.claim: The demonstrative may refer to the particular man or to the whole class of deniers who mistreat the weak under the influence of their predatory nature.
BURSEVI:v10p403/r5.anchor: فالذي للعهد ويحتمل الجنس فيكون عاما لكل من كان مكذبا بالدين

BURSEVI:v10p403/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r6.claim: The inward reading sees the aggressive self as dominant over the orphan-like heart, driving it from the path of spiritual nourishment.

QASHANI:107:1-3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:107:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:107:1-3/r2.claim: Driving away an orphan means harming and harshly shoving the weak through the excessive predatory soul.
QASHANI:107:1-3/r2.anchor: يؤذي الضعيف ويدفعه بعنف وخشونة لاستيلاء النفس السبعية وإفراطها

QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r3.claim: The orphan-pusher shoves him harshly and may also be denying him his rights.
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r3.anchor: يدع اليتيم } . يدفعه بجفوة ، ويقال : يدفعه عن حقه

QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r5.claim: The text quotes the saying that mercy is removed only from the heart of a wretched person.
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r5.anchor: ولا تنزع الرحمة إلا من قلب شقي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person who pushes away the orphan deprives the orphan of his rightful due.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ارايت الذي يكذب بالدين قال : يكذب بحكم الله . فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم قال : يدفعه عن حقه

IBNASHUR:107:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:2/r1.claim: Yaduʿ means to shove someone away violently and coercively, as in the verse about being driven toward Hell.

TUSTARI:107:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:107:2/r1.claim: The denier pushes the orphan away from the orphan's due right.

AKHFASH:v2p586/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p586/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p586/r2.claim: Yaduʿʿu al-yatīm means he pushes the orphan away from his right; the verb is daʿaʿtuhu, adaʿʿu.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r1.claim: Yaduʿ means to push away: the denier violently pushes the orphan from his due to take the property, or dismisses the orphan because he expects no reward for feeding him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r2.claim: He neither feeds the poor nor urges others to feed them because he denies the recompense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244/r2.anchor: ولا يحض على طعام المسكين أي لا يطعمه ولا يأمر بإطعامه لأنه مكذب بالجزاء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p540#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p540#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p540#4/r1.claim: Yaduʿ al-yatīm means he pushes the orphan away; the same verb describes people being pushed toward Hell.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p540#4/r1.anchor: {يدع اليتيم} يدفعه. وكذلك قوله: {يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا} (2)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.claim: The denier of recompense harshly oppresses the orphan, withholds the orphan's right, and neither feeds nor treats the orphan well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.anchor: هو الذي يقهر اليتيم ويظلمه حقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.claim: The question means: do you know who denies requital? If not, it is the one who harshly drives away an orphan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.anchor: والمعنى : هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو ؟ إن لم تعرفه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r5.claim: يدع means to push an orphan violently with cruelty and abuse, or to reject him with harsh rebuke.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r6.claim: An alternate reading يدع is understood as abandoning and neglecting the orphan.

MAJAZ:v2p313/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p313/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p313/r1.claim: Yaduʿ al-yatīm means he pushes the orphan; some lighten the form and explain it as ‘he leaves him.’
MAJAZ:v2p313/r1.anchor: «فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم» (2) دععته دفعته وبعضهم يقول: يدع مخففة : يتركه..

MUJAHID:v2p786/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p786/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p786/r1.claim: Mujahid says the orphan-denier pushes an orphan away from his rightful due and wrongs him.
MUJAHID:v2p786/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾ يقول يدفع اليتيم عن حقه ويظلمه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#2/r1.claim: The denier of recompense drives the orphan away harshly, treating him with roughness and insult.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359#2/r1.anchor: أ ى يدفعه دفعا عنيفا بجفوه وأذى ويرده ردا قبيحا

NAHHAS:v5p295/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r8.speaker: أبو رجاء
NAHHAS:v5p295/r8.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads yaduʿʿu with a light consonant, meaning he abandons the orphan.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء ( يدع اليتيم ) مخففة أي يتركه

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r7.claim: يدع means to push away; Ibn Abbas says the denier pushes an orphan away from his due, while Qatada says he subjugates and wrongs the child.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس. { فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } أي يدفعه عن حقه

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r8.claim: The passage recalls that pre-Islamic Arabs denied inheritance to women and children, claiming only warriors deserved property.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r8.anchor: أنهم كانوا لا يورثون النساء ولا الصغار

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r9.claim: A prophetic report promises Paradise for the Muslim who cares for an orphan until the child becomes self-sufficient.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r9.anchor: من ضم يتيما من المسلمين حتى يستغني، فقد وجبت له الجنة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.claim: Reports differ on dating: some call the whole surah Meccan, while others call its first three verses Meccan and the rest Medinan; Qutb calls the mixed account likelier.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.claim: Religion is not outward forms or ritual; worship matters only when sincere devotion produces good deeds and sound social conduct.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.anchor: إن هذا الدين ليس دين مظاهر وطقوس

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.claim: A verbal claim to Islam and performance of prayer or other rites do not prove faith; its signs must appear in the person’s conduct.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.anchor: ولقد يقول الإنسان بلسانه : إنه مسلم

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.claim: Faith, once settled in the heart, immediately moves a person to righteous action; failure to move shows that faith is absent.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.anchor: إن حقيقة الإيمان حين تستقر في القلب تتحرك من فورها

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.claim: The opening question summons anyone able to see to identify the person who denies the Judgment.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.anchor: إنها تبدأ بهذا الاستفهام الذي يوجه كل من تتأتى منه الرؤية ليرى

QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.claim: The Qur’an answers who denies the Judgment by pointing to the person who shoves the orphan and refuses care for the poor, surprising under conventional definitions of faith.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.anchor: ومن هو هذا الذي يكذب بالدين

QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r2.claim: The verb describes forcefully pushing the orphan, humiliating and harming the child.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r2.claim: If belief were genuine, the person would neither push the orphan away nor neglect urging food for the poor.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r2.anchor: وما كان ليقعد عن الحض على طعام المسكين

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.claim: True assent transforms the heart and prompts kindness and care for fellow humans who need protection.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.anchor: إنما هي تحول في القلب يدفعه إلى الخير والبر بإخوانه

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.claim: God asks for deeds that confirm words; words without confirming action are worthless before Him.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.anchor: إنما يريد منهم معها أعمالا تصدقها

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.claim: These opening verses state with unusual clarity the spirit of the creed and the nature of the religion.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.anchor: وليس أصرح من هذه الآيات الثلاث في تقرير هذه الحقيقة التي تمثل روح هذه العقيدة وطبيعة هذا الدين

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.claim: Qutb declines to debate juristic boundaries of faith and Islam: those govern legal transactions, while this surah states God’s measure of the underlying reality.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.anchor: فأما هنا فالسورة تقرر حقيقة الأمر في اعتبار الله وميزانه

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r1.claim: The denier is characterized by an active offense against the orphan and an omission of urging food for the poor; the causal fa says disbelief produces orphan abuse.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r1.anchor: ذكر في تعريف من يكذب الدين وصفين

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r2.claim: These two acts are examples, not an exhaustive list of the denier’s vices; each points to other bad acts and violates both revelation and human decency.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r2.anchor: كأنه تعالى ذكر في كل واحد من القسمين مثالا واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r3.claim: Yadu means pushing the orphan away with violence and harshness, as in the image of people being driven into Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r4.claim: Pushing the orphan includes unjustly withholding his right and property, refusing even nonobligatory consolation, and scolding, beating, or humiliating him.

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r5.claim: A reading without shadda can mean abandoning the orphan or inviting everyone else while leaving him out; a Prophetic report praises a table that includes an orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء يدع أي يتركه ، ولا يدعوه بدعوة

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r6.claim: A reading with final long waw can mean inviting the orphan ostentatiously but not feeding him, instead exploiting or coercing him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r6.anchor: وقرىء يدعو اليتيم أي يدعوه رياء ثم لا يطعمه

RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r7.claim: The doubled consonant in يَدُعّ signals habitual conduct, so the threat does not cover an isolated act followed by repentance; believers’ lapses are fleeting, unlike deniers’ persistence.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105#2/r7.anchor: يدع بالتشديد معناه أنه يعتاد ذلك فلا يتناول الوعيد

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.speaker: Muqātil and al-Kalbī
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.claim: They say the surah was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.anchor: Muqātil and al-Kalbī said, “This sūrah was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī”

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.speaker: Ibn Jurayj
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abū Sufyān struck with a stick an orphan who asked him for something while he was slaughtering his weekly camels, prompting revelation.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.anchor: Ibn Jurayj said, “Abū Sufyān was in the habit

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.claim: Even if first tied to one person, the accusation has general force; denying dīn, as religion or Judgment, underlies other sins and violations.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.anchor: Even if it was first recorded in reference to a specific individual, it still has a general implication

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r5.claim: Driving away orphans echoes criticism of consuming their inheritances.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r5.anchor: The accusation of driving away the orphan also alludes to the habit of devouring the inheritances of orphans

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r1.claim: The fa of fadhālika can answer an implied condition such as if you reflect or seek to know the person.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r1.anchor: أن الفاء جواب شرط مقدر، أي: إن تأملته، أو إن طلبت علمه فذلك

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it coordinates fadhālika with alladhi yukadhdhib; the answer to arayta is omitted, and the question asks whether denial, harming orphans, and neglecting the poor is commendable.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r2.anchor: أنها عاطفة " فذلك " على " الذي يكذب " إما عطف ذات على ذات، أو صفة على صفة. ويكون جواب أرأيت " محذوفا لدلالة

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r3.claim: Under the first parse the demonstrative is nominative, either as subject with the relative as predicate or as the predicate of an omitted subject with the relative as modifier; under the second it is accusative by coordination.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r3.anchor: فعلى الأول يكون اسم الإشارة في محل رفع بالابتداء، والخبر الموصول بعده، وإما على أنه خبر لمبتدأ مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r4.speaker: the Shaykh
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r4.claim: The Shaykh rejects accusative coordination as syntactically strange: the natural reading is a new nominative subject, while accusative requires repeating the verb and demonstrative awkwardly points to the prior object.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r4.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ رد الثاني فقال: " فجعل ذلك " في موضع نصب عطفا على المفعول، وهو تركيب غريب

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r5.speaker: the Shaykh
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r5.claim: He says fadhālika refers to the single denier, so it cannot coordinate one entity with another; the omitted answer to arayta is its second object, not an answer.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r5.anchor: وأما قوله " إما عطف ذات على ذات " فلا يصح لأن " فذلك " إشارة إلى الذي يكذب فليسا بذاتين

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r6.speaker: the Shaykh
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r6.claim: He objects that hamza does not enter upon naʿma or biʾsa because they are performative rather than declarative.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r6.anchor: والاستفهام لا يدخل إلا على الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r7.claim: The author answers that an interrogative context makes explaining the object of inquiry natural, unlike the Shaykh's example without a question.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r7.anchor: أن في الآية الكريمة استفهاما وهو " أرأيت " فحسن أن يفسر ذلك المستفهم عنه، بخلاف المثال الذي مثل به

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r8.claim: The demonstrative can point forward to the person described after it rather than back to the denier, as in an imperative followed by a description.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r8.anchor: بل مشار به إلى ما بعده كقولك: " اضرب زيدا، فذلك القائم

SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r9.claim: The author replies that this is a response to the preceding interrogative, as grammarians call it, rather than an ordinary declarative answer.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2/r9.anchor: النحاة يقولون: جواب الاستفهام، وهذا قد تقدمه استفهام فحسن ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r1.claim: To show that an interrogative can precede a performative, the author cites fa-hal ʿasaytum; what follows ʿasa is a response to the question.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r1.anchor: فإن " عسى " إنشاء، فما كان جوابا له فهو جواب لنا

SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r2.claim: The common yaduʿʿ has damma and doubled ʿayn, from pushing away; Ali, al-Hasan, and Abu Raja read yadaʿ with fatḥa and light ʿayn, meaning leave or neglect.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ العامة بضم الدال وتشديد العين من دعه، أي: دفعه وأمير المؤمنين والحسن وأبو رجاء " يدع " بفتح الدال وتخفيف العين، أي: يترك ويهمل

SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads wa-la yuḥāḍḍ, from muḥāḍḍa, meaning they do not urge one another; the root was discussed in al-Fajr.
SAMIN-DURR:107:2#2/r3.anchor: وزيد بن علي " ولا يحاض " من المحاضة وتقدم في الفجر

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r1.claim: The denier of judgment is the one who pushes the orphan away from his right and wrongs him; the verb means to drive someone from a right.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] قال: «يدفع حق اليتيم»

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the action as withholding the orphan's right.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r2.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] قال: «يدفع حق اليتيم»

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the person pushes the orphan away and does not feed him.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] قال: «يدفع اليتيم فلا يطعمه»

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r4.claim: Qatāda says the person subjugates and wrongs the orphan.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] «أي يقهره ويظلمه»

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the action as overpowering or oppressing the orphan.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] قال: «يقهره»

TAB-FULL:v24p659/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r6.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r6.claim: Sufyān glosses the action as pushing the orphan away.
TAB-FULL:v24p659/r6.anchor: عن سفيان، في قوله: {يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2] قال: «يدفعه»

ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r2.claim: Yaduʿ means to push, as in being violently pushed into Hell in 52:13; the orphan-denier pushes the orphan away from his rights.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r2.anchor: معنى يدع في اللغة يدفع، وكذلك قوله: (يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا).

ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r3.claim: Another reading is explained as leaving the orphan neglected and not caring for him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r3.anchor: تأويله فذلك الذي لا يعبأ باليتيم ويتركه مهملا

THALABI:v10p304#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p304#3/r6.claim: The verb yad'u means to overpower the orphan, rebuke him, and push him away from his due; al-daʿ is a harsh shove.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r6.anchor: أي يقهره ويزجره ويدفعه عن حقه، الدع: الدفع في جفوة.

THALABI:v10p304#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r7.speaker: أبو رجاء
THALABI:v10p304#3/r7.claim: Abu Raja reads yad'u as leaving the orphan and falling short in fulfilling his rights.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو رجاء يدع اليتيم أي يتركه ويقصر في حقه

THALABI:v10p304#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p304#3/r8.claim: The hypocrites leave prayer in private when people are absent and pray publicly when people are present.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة في السر إذا غاب الناس ويصلونها في العلانية إذا حضروا.

THALABI:v10p304#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p304#3/r9.claim: Mujahid explains heedlessness as being inattentive, forgetful, and careless about prayer.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r9.anchor: الآية، مجاهد: لاهون غافلون عنها متهاونون بها،

THALABI:v10p304#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r10.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p304#3/r10.claim: Qatada says the heedless person does not care whether he prayed or did not pray.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: ساه عنها لا يبالي صلى أم لم يصل.

THALABI:v10p304#3/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p304#3/r11.claim: The Prophet says this warning is better than receiving the whole world, describing one who neither expects reward when praying nor fears his Lord when abandoning prayer.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r11.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون: «الله أكبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r8.claim: The denier pushes the orphan violently and harshly away from his right, as one is thrust toward Hell; commentators say he oppresses the orphan and withholds the due.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r8.anchor: (قوله) (¬3): {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم} أي يدفعه عن حقه دفعا بعنف وجفوة كقوله: {يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا} (¬4)

WAHIDI-QT:107:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:107:2/r1.claim: He harshly pushes an orphan away from what is rightfully his.
WAHIDI-QT:107:2/r1.anchor: { يدع اليتيم } أي يدفعه بجفوة من حقه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r4.claim: Orphan abuse and neglect of the poor are examples; the verses select the most defining and destructive social-ethical conduct of the Meccan unbelievers, and are reported to have been revealed about As ibn Wail.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r4.anchor: âyetin, putperestlerin tipik şahsiyetlerinden olan Âs b. Vâil hakkında indiği belirtilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur says the broader purpose is to condemn cruelty and injustice as grave evils rooted in denial of religion, God's judgments, or afterlife responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.anchor: bu tür kaba ve haksız davranışları sergileyenleri kınamak ve bu yaptıklarının Allah katında en büyük kötülüklerden olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r6.claim: Orphans and the poor represent vulnerable people needing protection; despising, insulting, or shoving them violates the rights of society's weak.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r6.anchor: Yetim ve yoksul, toplumun zayıf ve himayeye muhtaç kesimlerini temsil eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r7.claim: Religion's great social aim is to build love, solidarity, sharing, and a human consciousness that shares hardship and happiness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r7.anchor: insanlar arasında sevgi ve dayanışmayı, paylaşmayı sağlamak, sıkıntıların da mutlulukların da paylaşıldığı bir insanlık bilinci

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r8.claim: The verses condemn such conduct and encourage believers to help the vulnerable, urge others to help, and establish charitable institutions for more effective, orderly, lasting support.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r8.anchor: ihtiyaç sahiplerine yardım konusunda başkalarını teşvik etmenin, hatta bunun için hayır kurumları oluşturarak sosyal yardımı

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi say the opening about one who denies Judgment and repulses the orphan was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Sufyan slaughtered two camels each week; when an orphan asked him for food, he struck the child with a stick, and the verses were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان أبو سفيان بن حرب ينحر كل أسبوع جزورين

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Verses 2–3 parallel the vice catalogue in 89:17–18, which condemns neglect of orphans and the poor, devouring inheritance, and love of wealth; an alternate reading occurs for the exhortation to feed the poor.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. den zu V.2.3 parallelen Teil des Lasterkatalogs in 89:17.18

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r2.claim: Food, orphans, and the poor recur together in the virtue list 90:13–16, with orphans and poor in 89:17–18, 93:9, 69:34, and 74:44, forming an early Quranic social-critical topos.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Es handelt sich dabei also um einen schon früh im Koran auftretenden sozialkritischen Topos

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r3.claim: The orphan and widow and the poor and wretched are stereotyped pairings in the Hebrew Bible, with examples in Exodus, Deuteronomy, Malachi, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Auf ähnlich stereotype Weise können in der hebräischen Bibel „Witwe und Waise“

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r4.claim: The New Testament likewise commends charity and feeding the poor, especially Matthew 25, where these acts are placed in an eschatological setting like this sura.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Die Verdienstlichkeit karitativer Taten und insbesondere der Speisung von Armen wird aber auch im Neuen Testament betont

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r5.claim: The notes also refer readers to related material on 93:9, 90:11–16, and the prophetic-ethical command to give full measure in 83:1–4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r5.anchor: S. a. die Anmerkungen zu 93:9 und zu 90:11–16

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r6.claim: Although yadaʿu from waḍaʿa is also transmitted, the majority yaduʿʿu is preferable because “shove away” is harsher and better fits the context and the following geminated root ḥaḍḍa.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:2-3:anmerkung/r6.anchor: Für die Mehrheitslesung yaduʿʿu spricht jedoch, dass das schärfere „wegstoßen“ inhaltlich angemessener scheint

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura systematically links religious beliefs and ritual actions with an individual’s moral conduct in daily life.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Sure etabliert systematisch einen Konnex zwischen religiösen Überzeugungen und kultischen Handlungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r3.claim: The answer equates deniers of judgment with people who push orphans away and do not urge others to feed the poor.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r3.anchor: Die in V. 2.3 gegebene Antwort setzt die Leugner des Gerichts dann mit Menschen gleich

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.claim: Awareness of the eschaton grounds social solidarity, a theme also found in 92:5–9; 104:1–3 depicts conduct when this eschatological awareness is absent.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.anchor: V. 1–3 stellen damit die beständige Gewärtigung des eschaton als Voraussetzung gesellschaftlicher Solidarität dar

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.claim: This future-oriented accountability complements 106’s past-oriented grounding of present ethics in God’s earlier favors.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.anchor: komplementiert die Vergangenheitsorientierung der früheren Sure 106

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p374/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p374/r1.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p374/r1.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads the orphan phrase as ‘the one who turns away from the orphan’; Ibn Jinnī glosses this as shunning and mistreating the orphan, close to the common sense of pushing him away.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p374/r1.anchor: معناه -والله أعلم- يعرض عنه ويجفوه، فهو صائر إلى معنى القراءة العامة:

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p399/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p399/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p399/r1.claim: Qatāda explains that the denier shoves, oppresses, and wrongs the orphan.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p399/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يدع اليتيم ﴾ قال يقهره ويظلمه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r1.claim: The fāʾ may mark causation: the following description results from the suspense created by the opening question.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r1.anchor: قيل للسبية وما بعدها مسبب عن التشويق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r2.claim: Alternatively, the clause answers an omitted condition: if you do not know the denier, that person is the one who repels the orphan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r2.anchor: وقيل واقعة في جواب شرط محذوف على ان ذلك مبتدأ والموصول خبره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r3.claim: The denier violently pushes the orphan away and rebukes him harshly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r3.anchor: هو الذي يدع اليتيم أي يدفعه دفعا عنيفا ويزجره زجرا قبيحا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r4.claim: The demonstrative in place of a pronoun signals contempt and may also indicate the reason for the judgment; the relative clause confirms the trait.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r4.anchor: ووضع أسم الاشارة موضع الضمير لدلالة على التحقير وقيل للاشعار بعلة الحكم أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r5.claim: Ali, al-Hasan, Abu Raja', and al-Yamani read the verb lightly, meaning that the person abandons, neglects, and shuns the orphan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p242/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله وتعالى وجهه والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني يدع بالتخفيف أي يترك اليتيم لا يحسن اليه ويجفوه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r6.claim: The denier forcefully oppresses the orphan and pushes him away from his due; daʿ means a harsh, violent push.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r6.anchor: يقهره ويدفعه عن حقه والدع: الدفع بالعنف والجفوة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.claim: The person who violently shoves the orphan may be Abu Jahl, who pushed away an orphan under his guardianship seeking his own property; or Abu Sufyan, who beat a child seeking meat after slaughtering a camel; or al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, or a miserly hypocrite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.anchor: وهو أبو جهل كان وصيا ليتيم فجاءه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه فدفعه، أو أبو سفيان نحر جزورا

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.claim: Yadaʿ is also read to mean that he leaves the orphan alone.

BINTSHATI:v2p185/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r5.claim: Daʿʿ is a forceful, harsh push; the Qur'an uses it here for treatment of an orphan and in al-Ṭūr for driving deniers toward Hell.
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r5.anchor: والدع الدفع العنيف مع قسوة وجفاء.

BINTSHATI:v2p186/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r1.claim: An orphan is a child who has lost his father.

BINTSHATI:v2p186/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r2.claim: Qur'anic references pair orphans with the poor and captive, with the lost and destitute, with travelers, and with enslaved people, showing sustained concern for vulnerable groups.
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r2.anchor: ولحظنا اقتران اليتيم في هذه الآيات، بالمسكين والأسير (الإنسان، والبلد) ، والضال والعائل (الضحى)

BINTSHATI:v2p186/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r3.claim: The Qur'an establishes the orphan's social right, ranking it after rights of God, the Messenger, and kin in some passages and after worship, parents, and kin in others.
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r3.anchor: مما اقتضى أن يقرر كتاب الإسلام حق اليتيم في المجتمع الإسلامي الصالح

BINTSHATI:v2p186/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r4.claim: Al-Fajr warns those who fail to honor the orphan; al-Māʿūn calls pushing away an orphan a sign of denying religion.
BINTSHATI:v2p186/r4.anchor: وفي (سورة الفجر) الوعيد الرهيب لمن لا يكرمون اليتيم.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r2.claim: Shoving an orphan reflects the arrogance that destroyed the people of the elephant; neglecting food for the poor reflects the miser's belief that his wealth will make him immortal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r2.anchor: فإن دع اليتيم من الكبر الذي أهلك أصحاب الفيل , وعدم الحض على إطعامه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r5.claim: The demonstrative refers to the hateful person far removed from good, who violently shoves and wrongs the orphan because God has removed mercy from his heart; only a wretched person loses that mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r5.anchor: { فذلك } أي البغيض البعيد من كل خير { الذي يدع } أي يدفع دفعا عنيفا بغاية القسوة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r6.claim: The Prophet's supplication asks God for good deeds, avoidance of wrongs, and love of the poor, illustrating the virtue of compassion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r6.anchor: ولذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم إني أسألك فعل الخيرات , وترك المنكرات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r7.claim: Mercy toward the weak signals goodness, harshness signals evil, and a person miserly with kind words is even less likely to give from his wealth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r7.anchor: كانت القسوة عليهم علامة على الشر , وكان من بخل باللين في قاله أشد بخلا بالبذل من ماله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r10.claim: By rhetorical omission, the shove in the first clause implies contempt in the second, while the urging in the second implies corresponding encouragement in the first; together they signal denial through injury to the weak and neglect of kindness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r10.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا أن علامة التكذيب بالبعث - إيذاء الضعيف والتهاون بالمعروف

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the denier drives the orphan away from his right.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} قال: يكذب بحكم الله {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم} قال: يدفعه عن حقه

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r6.claim: Abu Talib’s verse witnesses that daʿʿ can mean to push or deny someone their right; Ibn Abbas cites it in response to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: عز وجل {فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم}

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb glosses “drives away” as “pushes away.”
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب {يدع اليتيم} قال: يدفعه

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r8.claim: Qatada says the person mistreats the orphan.

TAB:107:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:2/r1.claim: The denier of the dīn pushes the orphan away from the orphan's right and wrongs him.
TAB:107:2/r1.anchor: فهذا الذي يكذب بالدين ،   هو الذي يدفع اليتيم عن حقه ،   ويظلمه

TAB:107:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r2.speaker: author
TAB:107:2/r2.claim: The verb daʿʿ means to drive someone away from his right; al-Ṭabarī illustrates it with the verb's inflected forms.
TAB:107:2/r2.anchor: يقال منه :  دععت فلانا عن حقه ،   فأنا أدعه دعا

TAB:107:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says he withholds the orphan's right.
TAB:107:2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   {  فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } قال :  يدفع حق اليتيم

TAB:107:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:107:2/r4.claim: Mujahid says he pushes the orphan away and does not feed him.
TAB:107:2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   في قول الله :  {  يدع اليتيم } قال :  يدفع اليتيم فلا يطعمه

TAB:107:2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:107:2/r5.claim: Qatada says he subdues and wrongs the orphan.
TAB:107:2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {  فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } :  أي يقهره ويظلمه

TAB:107:2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:107:2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says he subdues the orphan.
TAB:107:2/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  {  يدع اليتيم } قال :  يقهره

TAB:107:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:2/r7.speaker: سفيان
TAB:107:2/r7.claim: Sufyan says he pushes the orphan away.
TAB:107:2/r7.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله :  {  يدع اليتيم } قال :  يدفعه

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.speaker: أبو نواس
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.claim: Abu Nuwas recasts the al-Māʿūn lines in al-khafīf, changing the phrase to فذاك الذي as he fits them into his poem.
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.anchor: ضمنه أبو نواس في شعره ففصل وقال فذاك الذي وشعره

BURHAN:v2p114/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.claim: The section asks about Qur’anic phrases that coincide with metrical poetry, whether a full line, several lines, or a hemistich, while treating such coincidence as distinct from poetry.
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.anchor: فإن قيل فقد وجد فى القرآن ما وافق شعرا موزونا إما بيت تام أو أبيات أو مصراع

BURHAN:v2p114/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.claim: They say the opening of al-Maʿun scans in khafif.
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.anchor: ﴿ أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾ قالوا هو من الخفيف

BURHAN:v4p301/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p301/r1.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v4p301/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash permits omitting the fāʾ where Sibawayh requires it and cites وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون as evidence.
BURHAN:v4p301/r1.anchor: جوز حذف الفاء حيث يوجب سيبويه دخولها

BURHAN:v4p301/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p301/r6.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v4p301/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the fāʾ in فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم as an extra particle.
BURHAN:v4p301/r6.anchor: وجعل منه الأخفش ﴿ فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾

BURHAN:v4p301/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p301/r7.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p301/r7.claim: Sibawayh instead analyzes the fāʾ as the result of an omitted condition: if you wanted to rebuke him, then this is the one.
BURHAN:v4p301/r7.anchor: وقال سيبويه هي جواب لشرط مقدر أي إن أردت عليه فذلك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says yaduʿʿu al-yatim means pushing the orphan away from his due, and cites a line by Abu Talib.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: يدفعه عن حقه. واستشهد بقول أبي طالب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r2.claim: Al-Farra likewise explains the phrase as pushing the orphan away from his right and wronging him; the root indicates movement, pushing, and disturbance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r2.anchor: ومعنى {يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ} عند الفراء كالذي في المسألة: يدفعه عن حقه ويظلمه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r3.speaker: الطبري وابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r3.claim: Al-Tabari also reports 'subdues' and 'pushes away'; Ibn al-Athir explains pushing as expelling.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r3.anchor: وهو أحد الأقوال في تأويلها عند الطبري، ومعه: يقهره، ويدفعه. وفسر ابن الأثير الدفع بالطرد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.claim: The author prefers coercive, harsh pushing with rebuke over merely withholding an orphan's right: in 52:13 the deniers are thrust into Hell despite having no right being denied.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.anchor: ولاحق فيها للمكذبين يُدَعُّون عنه ويدفعون، وإنما الدعُّ سَزْقٌ بقهرٍ ونهرٍ وغلظة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r5.claim: An orphan can be treated harshly even if his property is paid; fulfilling the formal entitlement alone does not excuse rejecting him rudely, as al-Asas defines the phrase as pushing him harshly.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r5.anchor: قد يكون مع عدم دفعه عن حقه وظلمه، وقد يتصور بعض الناس أنهم إذا أدوا لليتيم حقه وماله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.claim: The one who repels an orphan is described as denying religion, in contrast with God’s sheltering the Prophet when he was an orphan.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p505/r1.anchor: دعَّ اليتيم في الآية تكذيباً بالدين. وفيما مَنَّ به الله تعالى على نبيه المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj’s occasion report says Abū Sufyān sacrificed a camel weekly; when an orphan asked for something, he rebuffed the child with a stick.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.anchor: كان ينحر في كل أسبوع جزوراً ،   فأتاه يتيم فسأله شيئاً فقرعه بعصا ،   أقوال آخرها لابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r1.claim: Yaduʿʿu means to shove the orphan away harshly, with coldness or injury.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r1.anchor: { يدع اليتيم } : أي يدفعه دفعاً عنيفاً بجفوة أو أذى

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r3.claim: The sūra makes withholding kindness and harming the vulnerable signs of denying requital.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r3.anchor: جعل علم التكذيب بالجزاء ،   منع المعروف والإقدام على إيذاء الضعيف

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r4.claim: The majority read yaduʿʿu with ḍamma on dāl and a doubled ʿayn.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { يدع } بضم الدال وشد العين

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r5.speaker: علي والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r5.claim: ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and al-Yamānī read with fatḥa on dāl and an undoubled ʿayn, meaning to leave or neglect the orphan.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r5.anchor: وعلي والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني : بفتح الدال وخف العين ،   أي يتركه بمعنى لا يحسن إليه ويجفوه

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī proposes coordinating fa-dhālika with alladhī yukadhdhib, deleting arayta’s second object and using the following woe as its indication.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : بعد أن قدم فيما نقلناه من كلامه ما يدل على أن { فذلك الذي يدع } في موضع رفع ،   قال : وطريقة أخرى

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s accusative coordination is an unusual construction; the immediate, more eloquent parse makes fa-dhālika a nominative subject.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.anchor: فجعل فذلك في موضع نصب عطفاً على المفعول ،   وهو تركيب غريب

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.claim: The proposed coordination of one entity with another is invalid: fa-dhālika points to the same individual as alladhī yukadhdhib.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.anchor: لأن فذلك إشارة إلى الذي يكذب ،   فليسا بذاتين

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.claim: What al-Zamakhsharī calls an omitted answer to arayta is not an answer; it occupies the place of arayta’s second object.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.anchor: بل هو في موضع المفعول الثاني لأرأيت

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.claim: The interrogative hamza cannot enter نعم or بئس, which are performative expressions rather than statements.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.anchor: فهمزة الاستفهام لا نعلم دخولها على نعم ولا بئس ،   لأنهما إنشاء

ALUSI:107:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:2/r1.claim: One view makes the fāʾ causal, following the preceding inducement to discover the denier.
ALUSI:107:2/r1.anchor: قيل للسببية وما بعدها مسبب عن التشويق

ALUSI:107:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:2/r2.claim: Another analysis supplies an omitted condition: if you do not know the denier of recompense or Islam, he is the one who violently pushes the orphan.
ALUSI:107:2/r2.anchor: وقيل واقعة في جواب شرط محذوف على أن ذلك مبتدأ والموصول خبره

ALUSI:107:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:2/r3.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to drive the orphan away violently and rebuke him badly.
ALUSI:107:2/r3.anchor: هو الذي يدع اليتيم أي يدفعه دفعاً عنيفاً ويزجره زجراً قبيحاً

ALUSI:107:2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:2/r4.claim: The demonstrative replaces a pronoun to belittle the person, or to signal the reason for the judgment.
ALUSI:107:2/r4.anchor: ووضع اسم الإشارة موضع الضمير للدلالة على التحقير وقيل للإشعار بعلة الحكم أيضاً

ALUSI:107:2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:2/r5.claim: The relative construction signals that the attached description is established and certain.
ALUSI:107:2/r5.anchor: وفي الاتيان بالموصول من الدلالة على تحقق الصلة ما لا يخفي

ALUSI:107:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:2/r6.speaker: علي والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني
ALUSI:107:2/r6.claim: ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and al-Yamānī read yaduʿ with a light dāl: he abandons the orphan, shows no kindness, and shuns him.
ALUSI:107:2/r6.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه والحسن وأبو رجاء واليماني يدع بالتخفيف أي يترك اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r13.claim: One identifies the denier as Abū Jahl, who supposedly pushed away an orphan under his guardianship when the child asked him for his own property.
ALUSI:107:7/r13.anchor: وقيل هو أبو جهل وكان وصياً ليتيم فأتاه عرياناً يسأله من مال نفسه

ALUSI:107:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI:107:7/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies him as Abū Sufyān, who struck with a stick an orphan asking for meat from a camel he had slaughtered.
ALUSI:107:7/r14.anchor: وقال ابن جريج هو أبو سفاين نحر جزوراً فسأله يتيم لحماً

ALUSI:107:7/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r15.claim: Other identifications name al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾid, or a miserly hypocrite.
ALUSI:107:7/r15.anchor: وقيل الوليد بن المغيرة وقيل العاص بن وائل وقيل عمرو بن عائد وقيل منافق بخيل

ALUSI:107:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91.
ALUSI:107:7/r17.anchor: فكأنه قيل أخبرني ما تقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذون اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r21.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:107:7/r21.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that causal coordination making both clauses one group yields an awkward construction; the demonstrative is unnecessary and less natural than a relative clause or direct coordination.
ALUSI:107:7/r21.anchor: واعترض أبو حيان ذلك الوجه بأن التركيب عليه تركيب غريب

ALUSI:107:7/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r22.claim: Another view treats the demonstrative as an emphatic insertion pointing to the person's extreme distance in evil and corruption.
ALUSI:107:7/r22.anchor: وقيل إن اسم الإشارة هنا مقحم للإشارة إلى بعد المنزلة في الشر والفساد

ALUSI:107:7/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r23.claim: A further analysis coordinates two entities and asks whether the deniers and orphan-pushers are in a good or bad state; al-Kashf objects that the pronoun cannot naturally refer to both groups and be replaced by worshippers.
ALUSI:107:7/r23.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يكون العطف عطف ذات على ذات فالاستخبار عن حال المكذبين وحال الداعين

BAGHAWI:107:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:107:2/r1.claim: He oppresses the orphan and drives him away from his due right.
BAGHAWI:107:2/r1.anchor: يقهره ويدفعه عن حقه ، والدع : الدفع بالعنف والجفوة

BAGHAWI:107:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:107:2/r2.claim: Daʿ means pushing with violence and harshness.

BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.claim: Alladhī may be generic or refer to a known individual; the following verse supports the definite, known-person reading.
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.anchor: و( الذي ) يحتمل الجنس والعهد ، ويؤيد الثاني قوله{ فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم }

BAYDAWI:107:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:2/r1.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to shove the orphan away violently.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r1.anchor: يدفعه دفعا عنيفا ، وهو أبو جهل

BAYDAWI:107:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:2/r2.claim: One identification is Abu Jahl, guardian to an orphan who came unclothed seeking his own property and was shoved away.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r2.anchor: وهو أبو جهل ، كان وصيا ليتيم فجاءه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه فدفعه

BAYDAWI:107:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:2/r3.claim: Another account identifies Abu Sufyan: after he slaughtered a camel, an orphan asked for meat and he struck the child with his stick.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r3.anchor: أو أبو سفيان نحر جزورا فسأله يتيم لحما فقرعه بعصاه

BAYDAWI:107:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:2/r4.claim: Other identifications are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or a miserly hypocrite.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r4.anchor: فقرعه بعصاه ، أو الوليد بن المغيرة ، أو منافق بخيل

BAYDAWI:107:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:2/r5.claim: A further view takes the figure as a miserly hypocrite in general.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r5.anchor: أو الوليد بن المغيرة ، أو منافق بخيل

BAYDAWI:107:2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:2/r6.speaker: قرئ
BAYDAWI:107:2/r6.claim: An alternative reading yadʿ means to leave the orphan.
BAYDAWI:107:2/r6.anchor: أو منافق بخيل . وقرئ ( يدع ) أي يترك

BIQAI:107:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:2/r1.claim: The generic denier may hide his disbelief, but signs growing from its root expose him.
BIQAI:107:2/r1.anchor: من عمود الكفر الذي صدر به ويتفرع منه تفضحهم

BIQAI:107:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:2/r2.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to shove violently and cruelly; the person wrongs the orphan and does not urge others to honor him.
BIQAI:107:2/r2.anchor: أي يدفع دفعاً عنيفاً بغاية القسوة

BIQAI:107:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:2/r3.claim: God has removed mercy from such a person's heart, a mark of wretchedness; fear of God is the only motive for kindness, so denying requital hardens him.
BIQAI:107:2/r3.anchor: لأن الله تعالى نزع الرحمة من قلبه ، ولا ينزعها إلا من شقي ؛ لأنه لا حامل على الإحسان إليه إلا الخوف من الله سبحانه وتعالى

DURR:107:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:107:2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains yaduʿʿ as pushing the orphan away from his due, answering Nāfiʿ b. al-Azraq’s question about Arab usage.
DURR:107:2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له : أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل { فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } قال : يدفعه عن حقه

DURR:107:2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:2/r2.speaker: أبو طالب
