DURR:107:2/r2.claim: Abū Ṭālib’s cited verse uses yaduʿʿ for pushing aside weaker children while allotting an orphan his due, supporting Ibn ʿAbbās’s gloss.
DURR:107:2/r2.anchor: أما سمعت أبا طالب يقول : يقسم حقاً لليتيم ولم يكن

DURR:107:2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:2/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR:107:2/r3.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb glosses yaduʿʿ al-yatīm as pushing the orphan away.
DURR:107:2/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب { يدع اليتيم } قال : يدفعه .

DURR:107:2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:2/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:107:2/r4.claim: Qatāda says the person who pushes the orphan away is wronging him.
DURR:107:2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { يدع اليتيم } قال : يظلمه .

IBNATIYYA:107:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r1.claim: The description invites the hearer to look for these bad traits in the person.
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r1.anchor: أي ارقب فيه هذه الخلال السيئة تجدها

IBNATIYYA:107:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r2.claim: Yadʿu al-yatim means to push the orphan roughly.

IBNATIYYA:107:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r3.claim: The rough pushing may mean withholding food and kindness, or violating the orphan's rights and property; the latter is worse.
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r3.anchor: وذلك إما أن يكون المعنى عن إطعامه والإحسان إليه ، وإما أن يكون عن حقه وماله ، فهذا أشد

IBNATIYYA:107:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r4.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r4.claim: Abu Raja reads yadaʿ with a light dāl and fatḥa, meaning he does not treat the orphan well.
IBNATIYYA:107:2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء : «يدَع »- بفتح الدال خفيف- بمعنى لا يحسن إليه

IBNKATHIR:107:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:2/r1.claim: He forcefully oppresses the orphan and withholds the orphan's due, neither feeding nor treating him well.
IBNKATHIR:107:2/r1.anchor: هو الذي يقهر اليتيم ويظلمه حقه ، ولا يطعمه ولا يحسن إليه

KASHSHAF:107:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:2/r1.claim: The denier of recompense drives the orphan away roughly and harmfully, rejecting the child with harsh rebuke.
KASHSHAF:107:2/r1.anchor: هو الذي { يَدُعُّ اليتيم } أي : يدفعه دفعا عنيفا بجفوة وأذى

KASHSHAF:107:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:2/r2.claim: An alternative reading without gemination, yadaʿ, means leaving and neglecting.

KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.claim: The preceding warning powerfully shows that sin signals weak faith and loose certainty; the text then adds a warning of woe for those who pray.
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.anchor: وما أبلغه في التحذير من المعصية ،   وأنها جديرة بأن يستدل بها

KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.claim: Another syntax coordinates fa-dhālika with the denier, as a noun or description; the answer to “Have you seen?” is omitted and indicated by what follows, and the plural denotes the generic singular.
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.anchor: وطريقة أخرى : أن يكون { فَذَلِكَ } عطفاً على { الذي يُكَذّبُ }

MAWARDI:107:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:107:2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase with the wording يحقر البيت, in context describing the way the orphan is treated.
MAWARDI:107:2/r1.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى يحقر البيت ، قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI:107:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:107:2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the person wrongs the orphan.

MAWARDI:107:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:2/r3.claim: A third gloss is pushing the orphan away harshly, as in 52:13 where people are driven to Hell with a shove.
MAWARDI:107:2/r3.anchor: الثالث : يدفع اليتيم دفعاً شديداً ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { يوم يُدَعُّونَ إلى نارِ جهنَّمَ دعّاً }

MAWARDI:107:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:107:2/r4.claim: One explanation is that the person unjustly deprives the orphan of his right and property out of greed.
MAWARDI:107:2/r4.anchor: أحدهما : يدفعه عن حقه ، ويمنعه من ماله ، ظلماً له ، وطمعاً فيه ، قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI:107:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:2/r5.claim: Another explanation is that he pushes the orphan away to exclude and rebuke him.

MAWARDI:107:2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:2/r6.claim: A lightened reading, yadaʿu al-yatim, is also reported; on it he abandons the orphan and ignores him.
MAWARDI:107:2/r6.anchor: وقد قرئ " يَدَعُ اليَتيم " مخففة ، وتأويله على هذه القراءة يترك اليتيم فلا يراعيه

MAWARDI:107:2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:2/r7.claim: On the lightened reading, another possibility is that he forcibly uses and humiliates the orphan, acting arrogantly.
MAWARDI:107:2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل على هذه القراءة تأويلاً ثالثاً : يدع اليتيم لاستخدامه وامتهانه قهراً واستطالة .

NASAFI:107:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:2/r1.claim: The denier of the recompense violently shoves the orphan away, treating him harshly and abusively, and drives him off with rude rebuke.
NASAFI:107:2/r1.anchor: أي يدفعه دفعاً عنيفاً بجفوة وأذى

QURTUBI:107:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:2/r1.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to push away, as in 52:13, where people are driven toward Hell.
QURTUBI:107:2/r1.anchor: و " يدع " أي يدفع ،   كما قال : { يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا }

QURTUBI:107:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:2/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that he pushes the orphan away from his right.
QURTUBI:107:2/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس : { فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } أي يدفعه عن حقه

QURTUBI:107:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:2/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:107:2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the person oppresses and wrongs the orphan; the meanings are close.

QURTUBI:107:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:2/r4.claim: As discussed in al-Nisāʾ, people denied women and children inheritance, claiming only those who fight with spear and sword should control wealth.
QURTUBI:107:2/r4.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة " النساء " {[16465]} أنهم كانوا لا يورثون النساء ولا الصغار

QURTUBI:107:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:2/r5.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI:107:2/r5.claim: The Prophet says whoever shelters a Muslim orphan until the orphan is self-sufficient is guaranteed Paradise; no grading is stated here.
QURTUBI:107:2/r5.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم أنه قال : " من ضم يتيما من المسلمين حتى يستغني

RAZI:107:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:107:2/r1.claim: The orphan-pushing is the first of two traits identifying the denier of religion, and it is an outward action.
RAZI:107:2/r1.anchor: ذكر في تعريف من يكذب الدين وصفين ( أحدهما ) : من باب الأفعال وهو قوله
